definition: a player who primarily handles the ball and directs the team's offense.
A defensive position in basketball, where a player defends two opposing players.
Teams enter the bonus when they have committed a certain number of fouls, allowing the opposing team to shoot free throws for each subsequent foul.
A shot that is not attempted by the shooter, but is instead awarded to the team after a foul.
A quick offensive play where a team moves the ball up the court rapidly to score before the defense can set up.
A play in which one player throws the ball near the basket, and another player jumps, catches it mid-air, and scores in a single motion.
A performance in which a player accumulates a double-digit number in three statistical categories, such as points, rebounds, and assists.
An offensive play where a player sets a screen (the pick) for a teammate handling the ball and then rolls towards the basket to receive a pass.
A defensive strategy where players cover specific areas of the court rather than marking individual opponents.
A situation where a player is fouled while making a basket and is awarded a free throw.
